en: Oh? Weren't you the one who turned down my job offer?
Let me get this straight. Are you really offering a million an hour?
Yes, precisely. If you would escort a certain lady around town, I will assure you a million's worth of compensation.
Well? Will you accept this job?

I will, I will! Please let me take this job, I'm so broke!
Er, what I meant by that is... I, Tatsuo Shinada, pledge
to guard the lady with my life!
Very good. Thank you. Now please take a look behind you.
Uh... Okay.
Holy moly!

She is the lady I represent. The American songstress
turned global superstar, Daddy Papa!
Daddy... <Italic>Papa</Italic>?
Oh? You don't know of her? You must be joking.
Nope. Never heard of her. She really that famous?
You've never heard of Daddy Papa? The irresistible, international sensation? Sales of over seventy million CDs worldwide?
Oh... Huh. What makes a huge celebrity like her want to come all the way out here?
Well, she's always been appreciative of Japanese culture. So far, she's explored our major cultural hubs such as Tokyo and Osaka.
This time, she's traveling incognito so she can explore Nagoya unfettered.

You call that dumpster ensemble incognito? I mean, what is
that dress she's wearing? It smells like the ocean... Yikes!
That's real seaweed!

Just what part of America do you come from? I'd really like
to know where that getup would go unnoticed...
To be honest, I concur. However, as far as she's concerned, this is more restrained than her usual attire.
Ach! C'est humiliating to appear before others in a dress so somber and lacking in esprit. Were there a pit, I would hide in it in shame.
Oh, what? You speak Japanese?
Daddy is capable of conversing in four languages, Japanese being one. The French she peppers in is mostly for show.
Ah, oui! The languages of the world, they give inspiration to the poems that I write. Japanese c'est mon favorite especially.
Daddy is a true musical prodigy. She not only composes all her songs, she writes all the lyrics as well.
Unfortunately, she's suffering from a bit of writer's block with the lyrics for her new song. She's visiting in hopes of finding inspiration.
Bite your tongue! I do not wish to be hearing of that now, understand? Now, you are to be guiding me, Mister...?
Shinada, ma'am. Tatsuo Shinada, at your service.
Very well, Tatsuo, enchantée. As you have heard, Daddy Papa I am. I shall be granting you permission to address me as "Your Ladyship."
Your Ladyship. O-kay...
Please excuse me for not introducing myself earlier. I'm George Matsuno. I'm Daddy's secretary and bodyguard.
Oh? Matsuno, that is too formal. A pet, you are.
Yes, well... Perhaps that might be more accurate.
It's not easy being you, is it?

I'm afraid not. Moreover, Nagoya is completely new to me,
despite the fact I grew up in Japan.
Ah, got it. So that's why you needed a tour guide.
Yes. There's also the fact that Daddy can't stay long. If she is in public too long, it could cause a media circus.
Anyway, without further ado, I'd like you to recommend a good place to start with. I will handle the security.
A good place? You mean, like, a tourist spot?
Oui! But, I am a superstar international. Take me you shall to a sight that is worthy of being seen by mine eyes.
Hmm. Okay. But... where would that be?
(The TV Tower would be the safe choice.)
All right, let me show you the way. Please follow me.
(Maybe I could show her Club Futo Momo. I think it's pretty snazzy, and who knows? A touch of titillation might help break the ice.)
(Maybe she'll like the view from the Oval Stage lookout.)
What's the problem? You're just gonna blow it on lame otaku bullshit.

We'll put it to better use. So hurry up and fork it over.
Unless you want your waifu to get hurt, hahaha!
Please... just leave me alone...
We'll leave you alone once you hand over the money. Fuckin' nerd.

Say, guys. Don't you think you're being a little obvious
here, shaking down this kid in broad daylight? You know
the police don't look too kindly on that sort of thing.
Maybe he's the geek's best buddy. Bet they were about to watch hentai together!
No, on both counts. But for a couple of haters, you sure know a lot about his hobbies.

Heh. That's just our way of getting inside his head.
Bullying's all about psychological warfare, man.
And guess what. We saved the guerilla warfare for you. Hope you don't mind us goin' apeshit!
Five of ya, that's the best you can do?
Here. It's yer money. Now get goin'. Ya heard what they said; ya don't wanna be seen with me.
You're... an escaped convict for real?
I see... Saejima-san, that doesn't change the fact that you saved my life. And I... I have to believe you had a good reason to break out of prison.
You don't seem like someone who would do that out of selfishness.
Kayama-han...
Um, could you wait here a moment?
I can, but why?
I'll be right back!
What were ya doin'?
I couldn't let you go without thanking you...
You got a pack of <Color:8>High-grade Cigarettes<Color:Default>.
...Ya went and bought this for me? But ya need yer money for Tokyo.
Haha, that's true. But I needed to show you how I feel. It's not much, but it's the best I can do.
It's great. In fact, nothin's ever made me feel more grateful. Thanks.
Damn, it's the cops. All right, Kayama-han. Hope things work out for ya in Tokyo.
Please take care of yourself!
Assholes! Give it back!
Shut up, ya loser! What's a homeless guy need with cash anyway? Think of us working folks who pay for our own shit.
Yeah, look how much he's got. 10,000 yen in loose change! Haha, he musta been saving up every handout for months!
That money's my train fare to Tokyo... Please.
What, you wanna go be homeless there, and be a nuisance to the good citizens of Tokyo? We can't allow that! We're being good Samaritans by taking this money!
I second that! It's better spent on our lunch, anyway!
You want something, dickwad?
Give the money back.
This ain't yer business.
Oh, shit! It's him, the dude who broke out of prison! He was on TV, remember?
Seriously? Hey, if we catch him ourselves, then we'll really be good Samaritans!
Good point! It'll be easy with five of us. Let's take him!
Hehehe, when everyone calls me a hero, Miki will finally drop her panties. This is my lucky day!
I'll show ya how lucky a day you're havin'. C'mon!
Hey! You all right?
(Gotta get some food into this fella.)
Hey, can ya eat this?
Hey, looks like you're feelin' better.
Thank you. I am feeling better. My name's Kayama, by the way.
I'm Saejima. Can't be easy bein' homeless in the snow.
Yeah... it's no winter wonderland for guys like me. The nights are just awful...
Can ya sleep?
Only if I'm exhausted. Then I try to find a spot with a roof... subway entrance or something... and bundle up in my blankets.
Even then, the cold is something terrible.
I try to stay awake all night. Sleeping during the day is safer, because you're less likely to freeze to death...
I've lived here a long time, but I can't keep this up. That's why I'm making my way to Tokyo. Warmer there. Maybe I could start over somehow.
Ya won't be as cold there, but the city's got more troublemakers, ya know. You okay for money?
Sometimes I get day labor jobs from the government, and I've been saving up. It's gonna cost me 10,000 yen to get to Tokyo. That's the goal.
If ya don't mind, I can help ya with money.
You've already helped me enough. But thanks for the offer.
I'm close to my goal, and I want to finish it on my own.
All right. Got it.
I've got work today, in fact. I should go now.
Sure. You take care.
(The man's freezin'... Gotta get some warm food in him.)
Ooh, the Japanese sake. Pure ambrosia from heaven. This... "tebasaki" as well. They are not the wings of chickens, but of angels.
I'm with you, Daddy. But go easy on the sake. You don't want to get so hammered that you can't even pick up a pen to write.
Aww, doesn't she deserve to have a little fun? After all, she went through all this trouble coming out here. Let's make it a night to remember!
Tatsuo, well said! Correct you are. Drink we must once more. Tatsuo, to what shall we toast?
Well, of course, to you, Daddy Papa.
That's a fine idea. I was about to suggest the same.
Ah, such darlings you are. Far across the ocean, here in Nagoya, I am toasted by two charming gentlemen. So fortunate I am!
This amazing life now, young me could never have imagined...
I propose we drink to your gorgeous eyes.
Ooh la la! Tatsuo, so very naughty you are. You mean to seduce me? It was not so very long ago you knew not even my name.
Hahaha, if we were staying longer, I could give you more time to bond, but I'm afraid that isn't possible this time around. My apologies.
An honor it is, to be so far from home in a land across the ocean, for its men to whisper sweet nothings about moi.
Hey, I know! Let's drink to that crazy dress of yours. After all, they say putting seaweed into sake makes it taste smoother.
...I see this dress has fallen into disfavor with you. However, I have no wish to give it up for you to make smooth your sake.
Shinada-san, please don't tease Daddy about the seaweed. She doesn't take well to slights about her fashion sense.
But... I wasn't teasing. I was teaching her something.
...No longer do I wish to drink. You may forget that toast.
Shinada-san, before she became a star, Daddy scraped by as a waitress. During that time, she wrote thousands of songs.
Thousands!? You sure you're not exaggerating here?
Not in the slightest. Back then, writing poetry was as natural as breathing. I think of myself then as an insect, petite and sans significance.
Acute and ravenous hunger drove me daily to seek the path of success.
Now, however, I am plagued by fear. Terror that I will be falling back down to failure.
Every morning I check in the mirror, making sure I have not devolved into a lowly worm from what was once a beautiful butterfly.
Dang. I guess even a goddess still has to face her demons.
Actually, Shinada-san, this is a great turn of events. Daddy's relaxed enough to open up and share her worries with us.
If this keeps up, she could very well snap out of her funk and break through her writer's block.
By the way, Tatsuo, really you have not heard my music?
Oh. Yeah, I'm sorry. I haven't.
Hahaha, someone like you is actually invaluable to us for market research. It's incredibly rare to find someone who has never heard of Daddy in this day and age.
Ergh... I wish I had a better excuse than "I'm just scraping by." But I can't exactly afford to make music a hobby.
Stay your worries. Burning you on a cross I am not. However, indeed it is rare for an ordinary person to be ignorant of Daddy.
Very well, Tatsuo, let me ask you this. To you, what kind of music do you think I am a singer of?
What kind of songs do you write? Hoo, let me think here. Uh...
I can imagine you singing songs to cheer on the weak. Like, songs to give courage to people who have no confidence in themselves.
I see. So that was your first impression, was it?
You are startling, Tatsuo. Your perception, it is perfection incarnate! ...Almost.
Wait, I was right?
Oui. For you see, I was not born this way. As a powerless plebeian, is how I started my life. So I sing to embolden the timid, much like my helpless former self.

I can see you belting out wicked rock anthems that tear down
the system. Can't imagine anything else, to be honest.
Hmm. Perhaps it is inevitable you should so picture me. Acquainted we have been for only so short a time.
...Did I say the wrong thing?
My music, it is songs to cheer on the weak. My desire, it is to embolden the timid at heart, much akin to my pre-celebrity persona.
I see you singing gentle songs of healing. Hope I'm not too far off the mark.
I see. So that's your first impression, huh?
The quality of healing, similarity there is un petit. However, my music, it is songs to cheer on the weak.

My desire, it is to embolden the timid of heart, people akin
to how I was before by shedding my weakness like snakeskin.
You can see from my dress of seaweed, I am conformist not at all. My character, being too strong, many times made an outcast of me.
However, success I achieved without betraying who I am.
I am one example of a sheep of color black who made society accepting on her own terms.
